A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same CLIP-GS work, and all 11 pages, equations, figures and tables are readable. Neither contains an appendix. V2 mentions supplementary visualizations that are not included; these cannot be credited as inspected additions.

before.justification: V1 reports original retrieval, zero-shot and few-shot classification results, component ablations, reconstruction measurements and model-scaling experiments.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results and reports a revised component ablation distinguishing position-and-color inputs from all Gaussian attributes.

M1.justification: Equation (4) corrects the written image-voting loss from contrasts with text embeddings to contrasts with image embeddings. This repairs the objective specification; it does not establish an implementation change. The tokenizer, encoder, voting mechanism and inference procedures remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Objaverse/Objaverse-XL training coverage, Objaverse-GS and ModelNet-GS evaluations, and retrieval, zero-shot and few-shot tasks. The illustrated real-image and two-image retrieval scenarios are also retained.

E2.justification: Table 5 removes the separately listed point-cloud Uni3D comparator scoring 47.7/69.8/77.3 and distinguishes position-and-color versus all-attribute fine-tuning controls. The comparator sets in the main retrieval and classification comparisons, Tables 1–4, are unchanged.

E3.justification: V1 describes the 46.9/68.5/75.9 fine-tuning result as using input expanded from 6 to 14 dimensions. V2 assigns those scores to position-and-color-only inputs and separately reports all-attribute fine-tuning. This revises the reported ablation settings without establishing that experiments were rerun. Main evaluation protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The revised Table 5 explicitly compares fine-tuning on position and color with fine-tuning on all Gaussian attributes, testing whether direct attribute inclusion helps. The ordering, initialization, reconstruction and model-scaling analyses remain present.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five independent experiments for few-shot standard deviations and retain the same uncertainty reporting in Table 3. No additional seeds, confidence intervals or statistical tests are reported.

E6.justification: The full-model rows in Tables 5–7 change from 48.6/70.6/77.8 to 48.5/70.3/77.5. Table 5 newly reports 44.8/66.3/74.1 for all-attribute fine-tuning. In Table 6, combined ordering consequently remains best on Top1 but falls below every single ordering on Top3 and Top5. Main benchmark results are unchanged.

T1.justification: Equation (4) changes both contrastive terms from text embeddings to image embeddings, correcting the mathematical definition of the image objective. The other equations are retained; no theorem, proof or additional derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims: unified 3DGS–image–text representations, efficient triplet generation and superior retrieval and classification performance. Local wording changes do not alter their scientific scope.

C2.justification: Section 5.4 newly interprets the drop from 46.9 Top1 with position-and-color fine-tuning to 44.8 with all attributes as evidence that directly adding Gaussian attributes can impair learning. V1 instead attributed the 46.9 result to learning the expanded Gaussian attributes.

D1.justification: Table 5 and its discussion revise the input documentation for the fine-tuning controls, explicitly distinguishing position-and-color-only inputs from all Gaussian attributes. Rendering, reconstruction and initialization details remain unchanged, with no new hardware, training-budget or code-access information.

R1.justification: Both versions retain the same 66 reference entries and the same positioning relative to point-cloud multimodal learning and 3D representations. Shortened descriptions and changed citation page references do not introduce new research relationships.

P1.justification: V2 tightens introductory and related-work prose, reorganizes the component-ablation explanation into labeled bullets, standardizes GS-CLIP to CLIP-GS in tables, and adds acknowledgments and supplementary-material pointers. The overall section structure is retained.

P2.justification: Table 5 is restructured with grouped fine-tuning rows and an expanded caption. Tables and text reflow, including relocation of Table 7 beside its discussion. The six figures retain their content; no new visual analysis is included.

improvement.justification: Correcting Equation (4) and distinguishing the fine-tuning controls in Table 5 improve mathematical correctness and interpretability. Revised full-model ablation scores also agree with Table 2. The gain is limited: Table 6 retains its favorable interpretation and bold emphasis for combined ordering despite its revised Top3 and Top5 scores falling below single-order alternatives.
